newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN MINISTER, KREDIETBANK PROBED IN TAX CASE.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN MINISTER, KREDIETBANK PROBED IN TAX CASE.

text.p: Belgian judicial police on Monday searched the offices of Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt in a probe into suspected tax fraud by Belgian banks and questioned staff of leading Belgian bank Kredietbank.

"The finance ministry confirms that there have been searches in the offices of cabinet members and of the administration, in the framework of a probe into operations done by certain banks, notably with regard to flat-rate taxes paid abroad," the finance ministry said in a statement.
Maystadt's personal office had not been searched, a ministry spokesman told Reuters.
Maystadt said earlier he did not know the purpose of the search.
"I have to find out what this is about. I am relaxed," Maystadt told RTL television.
In recent weeks, Maystadt has been dogged by reports in the Belgian press saying that he had been lenient to certain banks with regard to tax cases.
The judicial police also questioned staff members of Kredietbank NV , one of Belgium's top four banks.

"The judicial police has questioned staff members of our fiscal department. We do not yet know what this is about, it may have something to do with a bourse operations tax case or with our Luxembourg sister bank Kredietbank Luxembourg," a spokeswoman for the bank told Reuters.
Belgian media have reported that Maystadt had intervened with the tax administration in favour of Kredietbank.

A source close to the court told Reuters that Monday's two actions had been ordered by the same investigating team, but neither the finance ministry nor Kredietbank could confirm whether there was a link between the two investigations.
Maystadt has denied any wrongdoing with regard to his alleged intervention in favour of Kredietbank. Kredietbank also has repeatedly denied that its actions were fraudulent.
In recent weeks the bank has come under fire in Belgian media over allegations of tax evasion.
One case involves the so-called flat-rate tax on income from foreign investments.
In the late eighties, coupons on bonds from certain countries gave right to a flat-rate tax break, even if no taxes had been paid abroad.

Belgian media have said banks also passed on benefits from this tax loophole to their corporate clients. The Belgian tax authorities are now allegedly reclaiming bourse tax on the securities sold in this framework.
Kredietbank Luxembourg, Kredietbank's sister bank, has been the object of an investigation into tax avoidance schemes since last year.

Kredietbank shares closed 1.9 percent lower at 11,550 francs in high volyme of 15,644 shares. The raid on Maystadt's office also weighed on the Belgian franc, ended at 20.6315/25 to the mark, from 20.6293/03 on Friday.
